record.original_question: Let G be a hyperbolic group which is virtually compact special in the sense of Haglund–Wise. Suppose that the set of second Betti numbers of the finite-index subgroups of G is bounded. Must G be virtually either a free group or a surface group?

evidence.quote: Let G be a hyperbolic group which is virtually compact special in the sense of Haglund–Wise. Suppose that the set of second Betti numbers of the finite-index subgroups of G is bounded. Must G be virtually either a free group or a surface group?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a word-hyperbolic group that is virtually compact special in the sense of Haglund–Wise; that is, $G$ has a finite-index subgroup which is isomorphic to the fundamental group of a compact special cube complex (a non-positively curved cube complex whose hyperplanes satisfy: no hyperplane self-intersects, no hyperplane self-osculates, no two hyperplanes inter-osculate, and no two hyperplanes are directly self-osculating). For a finitely generated group $H$, let $b_2(H) = \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} H_2(H;\mathbb{Q})$ denote its second rational Betti number. Suppose that
$$\sup\{\, b_2(H) : H \le G,\ [G:H] < \infty \,\} < \infty.$$
Must $G$ be virtually free or virtually a surface group (i.e., must $G$ contain a finite-index subgroup isomorphic to a free group or to the fundamental group of a closed orientable surface)?
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears as a newly proposed problem in the 2026 Kourovka Notebook collection of open problems in group theory. Web searches did not surface any published solution; related work on virtually special hyperbolic groups, surface subgroups, and L²/Betti number growth (e.g., results on virtually free-by-cyclic groups and homology growth) is active but does not resolve this specific dichotomy. The problem is best regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: Virtually Free-by-Cyclic Groups (DPhil thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: Results on hyperbolic virtually compact special groups and their virtual fibering / free-by-cyclic structure, but not addressing the bounded virtual b_2 dichotomy.
status_evidence.claim: Related results exist but the precise dichotomy in the question is not established.

status_evidence.title: Homology Growth, Hyperbolization, and Fibering
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on homology growth of hyperbolic and cubulated groups.
status_evidence.claim: Active research on Betti numbers in finite-index subgroups of hyperbolic special groups, no resolution of the question found.
